readings: The assignment part of a getcall operation stores in and inout parameters, that of a getreply operation the return value (and out/inout parameters), and that of a catch operation the exception.
The assignment part of any procedure-based receiving operation stores only in and inout parameters, return values or exceptions.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: Strong typing IS NOT required for the message or parameter value assignment part of a receiving operation.
requirements.original: For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.

ambiguity.issue: "strong typing is not required" followed by "e.g. ... shall be type-compatible" is contradictory in wording; chosen reading: type compatibility instead of type identity is sufficient.
readings: The variable in a value or parameter assignment SHALL be type-compatible with, but need not be of the same type as, the received value.
No type check is performed for value or parameter assignments of a receiving operation.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The variable used for storing a received message SHALL be type-compatible with the type of the incoming message.
requirements.original: For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment part of a receiving operation MAY assign the sender address of a message, exception, reply or call to a variable.
requirements.original: In addition, the assignment part may also be used to assign the sender address of a message, exception, reply or call to a variable.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-assignment
requirements.canonical: Storing the sender address IS useful in one-to-many connections where the same message or call can be received from different components but the response has to be sent back to the original sending component.
requirements.original: This is useful for one-to-many connections where, for example, the same message or call can be received from different components, but the message, reply or exception shall be sent back to the original sending component.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.condition: the receiving operation uses any from a port array
requirements.canonical: For a receiving operation using `any from` on a port array, the assignment part MAY store the indices that identify the port instance where the receiving operation matched.
requirements.original: For receiving operations using the any port from a port array construction (see clause 22.2.2), the assignment part may also be used to store the indices that identify the specific port instance where the receiving operation matched.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.condition: the receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement
requirements.canonical: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the `@nodefault` modifier MAY be placed before it.
requirements.original: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the @nodefault modifier can be placed before it to indicate that the implicit alt statement containing the operation as an alternative shall have the @nodefault modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: a @nodefault modifier precedes a stand-alone receiving operation
requirements.canonical: If a `@nodefault` modifier is placed before a stand-alone receiving operation, the implicit `alt` statement containing the operation as an alternative SHALL have the `@nodefault` modifier.
requirements.original: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the @nodefault modifier can be placed before it to indicate that the implicit alt statement containing the operation as an alternative shall have the @nodefault modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: The `send` operation IS used to place a message on an outgoing message port.
requirements.original: The send operation is used to place a message on an outgoing message port.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: The `send` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `send` "(" TemplateInstance ")" [ `to` Address ].
requirements.original:
ObjectReference "." send "(" TemplateInstance ")" 
  [ to Address ]

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `to` clause of a `send` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef items or `all component`.
requirements.original: NOTE: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: The `send` operation places a message on an outgoing message port.
requirements.original: The send operation places a message on an outgoing message port.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: The message of a `send` operation MAY be specified by referencing a defined template or as an in-line template.
requirements.original: The message may be specified by referencing a defined template or can be defined as an in-line template.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: The optional `to` clause of a `send` operation CAN determine unicast, multicast or broadcast communication.
requirements.original: Unicast, multicast and broadcast communication can be determined by the optional to clause in the send operation.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.condition: one-to-one connection with unicast communication
requirements.canonical: The `to` clause of a `send` operation MAY be omitted in a one-to-one connection where unicast communication is used and the message receiver is uniquely determined by the test system structure.
requirements.original: A to clause can be omitted in case of a one-to-one connection where unicast communication is used and the message receiver is uniquely determined by the test system structure.

requirements.subject: ent:unicast-communication
requirements.canonical: A `send` operation uses unicast communication if the `to` clause addresses only one communication partner.
requirements.original: Unicast communication is specified, if the to clause addresses one communication partner only.

requirements.subject: ent:multicast-communication
requirements.canonical: A `send` operation uses multicast communication if the `to` clause includes a list of communication partners.
requirements.original: Multicast communication is used, if the to clause includes a list of communication partners.

requirements.subject: ent:broadcast-communication
requirements.canonical: A `send` operation uses broadcast communication if the `to` clause uses the `all component` keyword.
requirements.original: Broadcast is defined by using the to clause with all component keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `send` operation, and all parts of it, SHALL have a specific value.
requirements.original: a) The TemplateInstance (and all parts of it) shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: Matching mechanisms such as AnyValue SHALL NOT be used in the TemplateInstance of a `send` operation.
requirements.original: a) The TemplateInstance (and all parts of it) shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:in-line-template
requirements.condition: the message is defined in-line and its type is ambiguous
requirements.canonical: When the message of a `send` operation is defined in-line and the type of the message is ambiguous, the optional type part of the in-line template SHALL be used.
requirements.original: b) When defining the message in-line, the optional type part shall be used if there is ambiguity of the type of the message being sent.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: The `send` operation SHALL only be used on message-based ports.
requirements.original: c) The send operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the template to be sent shall be in the list of outgoing types of the port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: The type of the template sent by a `send` operation SHALL be in the list of outgoing types of the port type definition.
requirements.original: c) The send operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the template to be sent shall be in the list of outgoing types of the port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: The message-based communication operation 'send message' IS denoted by the keyword `send`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Send message; Keyword: send

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: The message-based communication operation 'receive message' IS denoted by the keyword `receive`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Receive message; Keyword: receive

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The message-based communication operation 'trigger on message' IS denoted by the keyword `trigger`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Trigger on message; Keyword: trigger

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The message-based communication operation 'check message received' IS denoted by the keyword `check`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Check message received; Keyword: check

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.condition: the port has a one-to-many connection
requirements.canonical: A `send` operation SHALL contain a `to` clause in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.original: d) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `to` clause of a `send` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `send` operation.
requirements.original: e) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the send operation.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: No AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `send` operation SHALL contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

ambiguity.issue: The consequence of a null AddressRef at runtime is not stated; chosen reading: it is a runtime error (test case error).
readings: Executing a `send` operation whose `to` clause contains a `null` AddressRef SHALL cause a test case error.
A `send` operation whose `to` clause contains a `null` AddressRef is undefined behaviour left to the tool.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: Applying a `send` operation to an unmapped or disconnected port SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: f) Applying a send operation to an unmapped or disconnected port shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `send` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: g) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `send` operation SHALL be of a data type.
requirements.original: h) _TemplateInstance shall be of a data type._

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `receive` operation IS the operation used to receive a message from an incoming message port queue.
requirements.original: The receive operation is used to receive a message from an incoming message port queue.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `receive` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `receive` ["(" TemplateInstance ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`value` (ValueRef | "(" {ValueRef [":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] FieldOrTypeReference] [","]} ")")] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]].
requirements.original:
[ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." receive
  [ "(" TemplateInstance ")" ] 
  [ from Address ]
  [ "->" [ value ( ValueRef| 
          ( "(" { ValueRef[ ":=" [ @decoded [ "(" Expression ")" ] ]
                 FieldOrTypeReference ][","] } ")" )
          ) ]
     [ sender ValueRef] 
     [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `receive` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.subject: ent:message
requirements.canonical: The message to be received by a `receive` operation MAY be specified by referencing a defined template or MAY be defined as an in-line template.
requirements.original: The message may be specified by referencing a defined template or can be defined as an in-line template.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `receive` operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue if, and only if, that top message satisfies all the matching criteria associated with the `receive` operation.
requirements.original: The receive operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue if, and only if, that top message satisfies all the matching criteria associated with the receive operation.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.condition: the match is not successful
requirements.canonical: If the match is not successful, the `receive` operation SHALL NOT remove the top message from the port queue.
requirements.original: If the match is not successful, the top message shall not be removed from the port queue i.e. if the receive operation is used as an alternative of an alt statement and it is not successful, the execution of alt statement shall continue with its next alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: the receive operation is an alternative of an alt statement and is not successful
requirements.canonical: If a `receive` operation used as an alternative of an `alt` statement is not successful, the execution of the `alt` statement SHALL continue with its next alternative.
requirements.original: If the match is not successful, the top message shall not be removed from the port queue i.e. if the receive operation is used as an alternative of an alt statement and it is not successful, the execution of alt statement shall continue with its next alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria of a `receive` operation are related to the type and value of the message to be received.
requirements.original: The matching criteria are related to the type and value of the message to be received.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The type and value of the message to be received are determined by the argument of the `receive` operation, derived either from a defined template or from an in-line template.
requirements.original: The type and value of the message to be received are determined by the argument of the receive operation, i.e. may either be derived from the defined template or be specified in-line.

requirements.subject: ent:in-line-template
requirements.canonical: The optional type part of the matching criteria of a `receive` operation SHALL be used to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being received.
requirements.original: An optional type field in the matching criteria to the receive operation shall be used to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being received.

ambiguity.issue: 'type field' is used for the optional Type ':' prefix of the in-line template, which restriction a) calls 'type part'; 'field' could be confused with a record field.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-attribute
requirements.canonical: Encoding attributes participate implicitly in matching by preventing the decoder from producing an abstract value from a received message encoded differently than specified by the attributes.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Encoding attributes also participate in matching in an implicit way, by preventing the decoder to produce an abstract value from the received message encoded in a different way than specified by the attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.condition: one-to-many connection
requirements.canonical: In the case of one-to-many connections, the `receive` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: In the case of one-to-many connections the receive operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The restriction of a `receive` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted using the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:one-to-one-connection
requirements.canonical: A one-to-one connection is considered a simple case of a one-to-many connection, so the `from` clause MAY also be used for a `receive` operation on a one-to-one connection.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.condition: the match is successful
requirements.canonical: If the match is successful, the `receive` operation removes the received message from the port queue.
requirements.original: If the match is successful, the value is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored in variables or formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.condition: the match is successful
requirements.canonical: If the match is successful, the received value or parts of it CAN be stored in variables or formal parameters.
requirements.original: If the match is successful, the value is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored in variables or formal parameters.

ambiguity.issue: 'is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored' mixes the always-happening removal with the optional storing; the 'and/or' scope is unclear. Chosen reading: removal always happens, storing is optional.
readings: If the match is successful, the message is removed from the port queue and the whole value or parts of it CAN additionally be stored in variables or formal parameters.
If the match is successful, either the message is removed from the port queue or parts of it are stored, or both.

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.canonical: Storing the received message or parts of it is denoted by the symbol `->` followed by the keyword `value`.
requirements.original: This is denoted by the symbol '->' and the keyword value.

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.condition: value is followed by a single variable or formal parameter name
requirements.canonical: When the keyword `value` is followed by the name of a variable or formal parameter, the whole received message SHALL be stored in that variable or formal parameter.
requirements.original: When the keyword value is followed by a name of a variable or formal parameter, the whole received message shall be stored in the variable or formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: A variable or formal parameter following the keyword `value` SHALL be type compatible with the received message.
requirements.original: The variable or formal parameter shall be type compatible with the received message.

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.condition: value is followed by a list enframed by parentheses
requirements.canonical: When the keyword `value` is followed by a parenthesized list, the whole received message and/or one or more parts of it CAN be stored.
requirements.original: When the keyword value is followed by a list enframed by a pair of parentheses, the whole received message and/or one or more parts of it can be stored.

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.canonical: For each element of a `value` redirect list that consists only of a variable or formal parameter name, the whole message SHALL be stored in that variable or formal parameter.
requirements.original: For each list element that consists only of a variable or formal parameter name the whole message shall be stored in that variable or formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: A variable or formal parameter that is a list element consisting only of a name in a `value` redirect list SHALL be of a type compatible with the type of the message.
requirements.original: The type of the variable or formal parameter shall be compatible with the type of the message.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: Each assignment notation member of a `value` redirect list stores the value of the field or element of the received message referenced on the right hand side of `:=` in the variable or formal parameter on the left hand side.
requirements.original: Each assignment notation member of the list allows storing the value of the field or element of the received message, which is referenced on the right hand side of the assignment notation (:=), in the variable or formal parameter on the left hand side.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: A variable or formal parameter on the left hand side of an assignment notation member of a `value` redirect list SHALL be type compatible with the type of the referenced field or element.
requirements.original: The variable or formal parameter shall be type compatible with the type of the referenced field or element.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: When assigning individual fields of a received message, encoded payload fields MAY be decoded prior to assignment using the `@decoded` modifier.
requirements.original: When assigning individual fields of a message, encoded payload fields can be decoded prior to assignment using the @decoded modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used
requirements.canonical: When the `@decoded` modifier is used, the referenced field on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring type.
requirements.original: In this case, the referenced field on the right hand side of the assignment shall be one of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: A field referenced with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: It shall be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: Failure of the decoding of a field referenced with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-encoding-parameter
requirements.condition: the referenced field is of universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the referenced field is of the universal charstring type, the `@decoded` clause MAY contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.original: In case the referenced field is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded` clause can contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-encoding-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL be of the charstring type.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-encoding-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-encoding-parameter
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause with a value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: The kind of error is not specified.
readings: A disallowed encoding format value SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
A disallowed encoding format value SHALL cause a compile-time error when it is known statically, and a test case error otherwise.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-encoding-parameter
requirements.condition: the referenced field is not of universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the referenced field is not of the universal charstring type, the optional encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.original: In case the referenced field is not a universal **charstring, the optional** parameter shall not be present.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@decoded` clause is typically used together with the `decmatch` matching mechanism in the matching part of the receive statement.
requirements.original: NOTE 5: The @decoded clause is typically used together with the decmatch matching mechanism in the matching part of the receive statement.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool CAN be optimized to call the decoder only once when a receiving statement contains both `decmatch` matching and `@decoded` assignment for the same payload field.
requirements.original: Since the decoding procedures for assignment and matching are virtually the same, TTCN-3 tools can be optimized in such a way that only one call to the decoder is made when the receiving statement contains both decmatch matching mechanism and @decoded assignment for the same payload field.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: The component reference or address of the sender of a received message CAN be retrieved and stored.
requirements.original: It is also possible to retrieve and store the component reference or address of the sender of a message.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Storing the sender of a received message is denoted by the keyword `sender`.
requirements.original: This is denoted by the keyword sender.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: the message is received on a connected port
requirements.canonical: When the message is received on a connected port, only the component reference is stored in the variable following the `sender` keyword.
requirements.original: When the message is received on a connected port, only the component reference is stored in the following the sender keyword, but the test system shall internally store the component name too, if any (to be used in logging).

ambiguity.issue: The sentence is garbled ('stored in the following the sender keyword'); the noun 'variable or formal parameter' is missing.

improper_terms.used: stored in the following the sender keyword
improper_terms.proper: stored in the variable or formal parameter following the sender keyword

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.condition: the message is received on a connected port
requirements.canonical: When the message is received on a connected port, the test system SHALL internally store the component name of the sender, if any, for use in logging.
requirements.original: When the message is received on a connected port, only the component reference is stored in the following the sender keyword, but the test system shall internally store the component name too, if any (to be used in logging).

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: A `receive` operation with no argument for the type and value matching criteria SHALL remove the message on the top of the incoming port queue, if any, if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.
requirements.original: A receive operation with no argument list for the type and value matching criteria of the message to be received shall remove the message on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: The `any port` keywords MAY be used with the `receive` operation to receive a message on any port.
requirements.original: To receive a message on any port, use the any port keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The `any from` PortArrayRef construct MAY be used with the `receive` operation to receive a message on any port of a specific port array.
requirements.original: To receive a message on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` PortArrayRef construct SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To receive a message on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirect
requirements.canonical: The index of the port in a single-dimensional port array at which the `receive` operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type integer.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a singledimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirect
requirements.canonical: The index of the successful port in a multi-dimensional port array MAY be stored in an integer array or record of integer variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a singledimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: When checking a port array for matching messages, the port indices are iterated from lowest to highest.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching messages, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.condition: the port array is multi-dimensional
requirements.canonical: If the port array is multi-dimensional, the ports are iterated from innermost to outermost array dimension, from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

ambiguity.issue: 'from innermost to outermost' could mean the innermost (last) index varies fastest, or that the innermost dimension is the outer loop; the example order [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1] supports the first reading, which is chosen.
readings: The last (innermost) index varies fastest: [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The first index varies fastest: [0][0], [1][0], [0][1], [1][1].

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all the criteria causes the `receive` operation to be successful, even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `receive` operation CAN be used as a stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.
requirements.original: The receive operation can be used as a stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: A stand-alone `receive` operation is shorthand for an `alt` statement with the `receive` operation as the only alternative.
requirements.original: In this latter case the receive operation is considered to be shorthand for an alt statement with the receive operation as the only alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:in-line-template
requirements.condition: the message is defined in-line and its type is ambiguous
requirements.canonical: When the message is defined in-line, the optional type part SHALL be present whenever the type of the message being received is ambiguous.
requirements.original: a) When defining the message in-line, the optional type part shall be present whenever the type of the message being received is ambiguous.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `receive` operation SHALL only be used on message-based ports.
requirements.original: b) The receive operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the value to be received shall be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: The type of the value to be received by a `receive` operation SHALL be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.
requirements.original: b) The receive operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the value to be received shall be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: A `receive` operation SHALL NOT bind incoming values to the terms of the expression or to the template.
requirements.original: c) No binding of the incoming values to the terms of the expression or to the template shall occur.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear what 'binding to the terms of the expression or to the template' means for a test author.
readings: Matching a received message SHALL NOT assign values to variables used in the template or expression (no unification-like binding).
Variables referenced in the template or expression SHALL NOT be changed by the receive operation except through the redirect clauses.

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.canonical: A `receive` operation without an argument (receive any message) SHALL NOT contain a `value` clause.
requirements.original: d) A message received by receive any message shall not be stored, i.e. the value clause shall not be present.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: e) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: Kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not specified.
readings: A type mismatch detectable statically SHALL cause a compile-time error.
A type mismatch SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the sender SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: e) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: Kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not specified.
readings: A sender type mismatch detectable statically SHALL cause a compile-time error.
A sender type mismatch SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error can happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible with the types in the assignment part, or if the `from` clause is missing but the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `receive` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port.
requirements.original: f) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the receive operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef in the `sender` clause of a `receive` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port.
requirements.original: f) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the receive operation.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: No AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `receive` operation SHALL contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef of an `any from` `receive` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: g) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirect
requirements.canonical: The index redirection SHALL only be used when the `receive` operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: h) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirect
requirements.condition: index redirection on a single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the array.
requirements.original: i) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional port arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirect
requirements.condition: index redirection on a multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the same as the dimension of the array.
requirements.original: j) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirect
requirements.condition: index redirection on a multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the type of the integer array or record of integer SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.original: j) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `value`, `sender` or `@index` clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to the variable is equal to the result produced by the `receive` operation.
requirements.original: k) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the receive operation i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the receive operation.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: Later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `value`, `sender` or `@index` clause does not lead to repeated invocation of the `receive` operation.
requirements.original: k) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the receive operation i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the receive operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: both from and sender clauses are present
requirements.canonical: If the `receive` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or formal parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the address expression in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: l) If the receive operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

ambiguity.issue: The from clause contains AddressRef items, not a template; 'parameter' should be 'formal parameter'.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: @decoded assignment of a field that is matched with decmatch
requirements.canonical: When a field stored with the `@decoded` modifier is matched with `decmatch` matching, the type of the template in the `decmatch` matching SHALL be type compatible with the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.
requirements.original: m) When assigning implicitly decoded message fields (by using the @decoded modifier) in cases where the value or template to be matched uses the MatchDecodedContent (decmatch) matching for the field to be stored, the type of the template in the MatchDecodedContent matching shall be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The referenced value or the return type of the function instance preceding the `receive` keyword SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: n) The referenced value associated with ValueRef or the return type associated with FunctionInstance followed by the receive keyword, shall be of a port type.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block uses ObjectReference, not ValueRef or FunctionInstance.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `receive` operation SHALL be of a data type.
requirements.original: o) TemplateInstance shall be of a data type.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `receive` statements.
requirements.original: p) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone receive statements.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation IS used to await a specific message on an incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The trigger operation is used to await a specific message on an incoming port queue.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `trigger` ["(" TemplateInstance ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`value` (ValueRef | "(" {ValueRef [":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] FieldOrTypeReference] [","]} ")")] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]].
requirements.original:
[ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." trigger
  [ "(" TemplateInstance ")" ] 
  [ from Address ]
  [ "->" [ value ( ValueRef| 
          ( "(" { ValueRef[ ":=" [ @decoded [ "(" Expression ")" ] ]
                 FieldOrTypeReference ][","] } ")" )
          ) ]
   [ sender ValueRef] 
   [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The trigger operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.condition: the top message meets the matching criteria
requirements.canonical: If the top message of the incoming port queue meets the matching criteria, the `trigger` operation behaves in the same manner as a `receive` operation.
requirements.original: If that top message meets the matching criteria, the trigger operation behaves in the same manner as a receive operation.

requirements.subject: ent:message
requirements.condition: the top message does not fulfil the matching criteria
requirements.canonical: If the top message of the incoming port queue does not fulfil the matching criteria of a `trigger` operation, the message SHALL be removed from the queue without any further action.
requirements.original: If that top message does not fulfil the matching criteria, it shall be removed from the queue without any further action.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation SHALL specify the port name and matching criteria for type and value.
requirements.original: The trigger operation requires the port name, matching criteria for type and value, an optional from restriction (i.e. selection of communication partner) and an optional assignment of the matching message and sender component to variables.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence says matching criteria are required, but clause 'Trigger on any message' allows a trigger without argument list. Chosen reading: the matching criteria are required unless the trigger on any message form is used.
readings: A `trigger` operation SHALL always specify matching criteria for type and value.
A `trigger` operation SHALL specify matching criteria for type and value unless it is a trigger on any message without argument list.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation MAY contain an optional `from` restriction selecting the communication partner.
requirements.original: The trigger operation requires the port name, matching criteria for type and value, an optional from restriction (i.e. selection of communication partner) and an optional assignment of the matching message and sender component to variables.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation MAY contain an optional assignment of the matching message and the sender component to variables.
requirements.original: The trigger operation requires the port name, matching criteria for type and value, an optional from restriction (i.e. selection of communication partner) and an optional assignment of the matching message and sender component to variables.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria defined in clause 22.2.2 apply also to the `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: The matching criteria as defined in clause 22.2.2 apply also to the trigger operation.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.condition: one-to-many connection
requirements.canonical: In the case of one-to-many connections, the `trigger` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: In the case of one-to-many connections the trigger operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The restriction of a `trigger` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted using the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:one-to-one-connection
requirements.canonical: A one-to-one connection IS a simple case of a one-to-many connection and allows the usage of the `from` clause in a `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-on-any-message
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation with no template instance SHALL trigger on the receipt of any message.
requirements.original: A trigger operation with no argument list shall trigger on the receipt of any message.

ambiguity.issue: 'argument list' is used for the optional TemplateInstance of the trigger operation.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-on-any-message
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation with no template instance IS identical in meaning to `receive` any message.
requirements.original: Thus, its meaning is identical to the meaning of receive any message.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: The `any port` keywords MAY be used in a `trigger` operation to trigger on a message at any port.
requirements.original: To trigger on a message at any port, use the any port keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The `any from` PortArrayRef syntax MAY be used in a `trigger` operation to trigger on a message at any port of a specific port array.
requirements.original: To trigger on a message at any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array-ref
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` `trigger` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To trigger on a message at any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: The index of the port of a single-dimensional port array at which the `trigger` operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type `integer`.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: The index of the port of a multi-dimensional port array at which the `trigger` operation was successful MAY be stored in an integer array or `record of integer` variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array
requirements.canonical: When a `trigger` operation checks a port array for matching messages, the iteration over the port indices IS from lowest to highest.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching messages, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array
requirements.condition: the port array is multi-dimensional
requirements.canonical: If the port array is multi-dimensional, the iteration over the ports IS from innermost to outermost array dimension and from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all criteria causes the `trigger` operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:message
requirements.condition: a port in the port array contains a non-matching message
requirements.canonical: If any port of the port array checked for matching contains a message that does not match, the `trigger` operation removes this message.
requirements.original: If any port in the port array which is checked for matching contains a message that does not match, this message is removed and the containing alt statement is re-evaluated, regardless of whether or not other ports in the port array would meet the trigger criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: a port in the port array contains a non-matching message
requirements.canonical: If any port of the port array checked for matching contains a message that does not match, the containing `alt` statement is re-evaluated regardless of whether other ports in the port array would meet the trigger criteria.
requirements.original: If any port in the port array which is checked for matching contains a message that does not match, this message is removed and the containing alt statement is re-evaluated, regardless of whether or not other ports in the port array would meet the trigger criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation CAN be used as a stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.
requirements.original: The trigger operation can be used as a stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.

requirements.subject: ent:stand-alone-trigger-statement
requirements.canonical: A stand-alone `trigger` statement IS shorthand for an `alt` statement with two alternatives, one expecting the message and one consuming all other messages and repeating the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: In this latter case the trigger operation is considered to be shorthand for an alt statement with two alternatives (one alternative expecting the message and another alternative consuming all other messages and repeating the alt statement, see ETSI ES 201 873-4 [1]).

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The rules of clause 22.2.2 for storing the received message, parts of the received message or the sender SHALL apply to the `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: Rules in clause 22.2.2 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation SHALL only be used on message-based ports.
requirements.original: a) The trigger operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the value to be received shall be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The type of the value to be received by a `trigger` operation SHALL be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.
requirements.original: a) The trigger operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the value to be received shall be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-on-any-message
requirements.canonical: A message received by a trigger on any message SHALL NOT be assigned to a variable.
requirements.original: b) A message received by TriggerOnAnyMessage shall not be assigned to a variable.

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value in a `trigger` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: c) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the sender in a `trigger` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: c) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the types in the receive part are not compatible with the types in the assignment part.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the `from` clause is missing but the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of type `address`, a component type, or the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port instance.
requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.

ambiguity.issue: 'component' is used where 'component type' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef item in the `sender` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of type `address`, a component type, or the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port instance.
requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.

ambiguity.issue: 'component' is used where 'component type' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array-ref
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef of a `trigger` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: e) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of a `trigger` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection used for single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the port array.
requirements.original: g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional port arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection used for multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the port array.
requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

ambiguity.issue: 'the dimension of the respective array' is read as the number of dimensions (supported by example 5: p[10][10] with v_i[2]).
readings: The size of the integer array SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the port array.
The size of the integer array SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection used for multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL allow storing the highest index of all dimensions of the port array.
requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is lazy or fuzzy
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `value`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `trigger` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable IS equal to the result produced by the `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the trigger operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the trigger operation.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.canonical: Later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable assigned in a `trigger` operation redirect SHALL NOT lead to repeated invocation of the `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the trigger operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the trigger operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: both from and sender clause present
requirements.canonical: If a `trigger` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the AddressRef in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: j) If the trigger operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

ambiguity.issue: 'template in the from clause' is used although the from clause contains AddressRef items (address or component references), not templates.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: k) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of a data type.
requirements.original: l) TemplateInstance shall be of a data type.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `trigger` statements.
requirements.original: m) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone trigger statements.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that invokes a procedure call.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that accepts a procedure call from a remote entity.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `reply` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that replies to a procedure call from a remote entity.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: The `raise` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that raises an exception to an accepted call.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getreply` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that handles the response from a previous call.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The `catch` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that catches an exception from the called entity.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that checks whether a call, exception or reply has been received.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation IS the operation that specifies the call of a remote procedure on another test component or within the SUT.
requirements.original: The call operation specifies the call of a remote operation on another test component or within the SUT.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `call` "(" TemplateInstance [ "," ( CallTimerValue | `nowait` ) ] ")" [ `to` Address ].
requirements.original:
ObjectReference "." call "(" TemplateInstance [ "," ( CallTimerValue | nowait ) ] ")" 
  [ to Address ]

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address of the `to` clause of a `call` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef items or `all component`.
requirements.original: NOTE: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation IS used to specify that a test component calls a procedure in the SUT or in another test component.
requirements.original: The call operation is used to specify that a test component calls a procedure in the SUT or in another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The information transmitted in the send part of a `call` operation IS a signature that is defined either as a signature template or in-line.
requirements.original: The information to be transmitted in the send part of the call operation is a signature that may either be defined in the form of a signature template or be defined in-line.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.condition: non-blocking procedure-based communication
requirements.canonical: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, exceptions to a `call` operation ARE handled by `catch` operations used as alternatives in `alt` statements.
requirements.original: In case of non-blocking procedure-based communication the handling of exceptions to call operations is done by using catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations as alternatives in alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.condition: the nowait option is used
requirements.canonical: If the `nowait` option is used in a `call` operation, responses and exceptions to the call ARE handled by `getreply` and `catch` operations used as alternatives in `alt` statements.
requirements.original: If the nowait option is used, the handling of responses or exceptions to call operations is done by using getreply (see clause 22.3.4) and catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations as alternatives in alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:response-and-exception-handling-part
requirements.condition: blocking procedure-based communication
requirements.canonical: In blocking procedure-based communication, responses and exceptions to a call ARE handled in the response and exception handling part of the `call` operation by means of `getreply` and `catch` operations.
requirements.original: In case of blocking procedure-based communication, the handling of responses or exceptions to a call is done in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of getreply (see clause 22.3.4) and catch (see clause 22.3.6) operations.

requirements.subject: ent:response-and-exception-handling-part
requirements.canonical: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation IS syntactically similar to the body of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The response and exception handling part of a call operation looks similar to the body of an alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:response-and-exception-handling-part
requirements.canonical: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation defines a set of alternatives describing the possible responses and exceptions to the call.
requirements.original: It defines a set of alternatives, describing the possible responses and exceptions to the call.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: An alternative of the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY be enabled or disabled by a Boolean expression placed between the "[ ]" brackets of the alternative.
requirements.original: If necessary, it is possible to enable/disable an alternative by means of a boolean expression placed between the "[ ]" brackets of the alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:response-and-exception-handling-part
requirements.canonical: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation IS executed like an `alt` statement without any active default.
requirements.original: The response and exception handling part of a call operation is executed like an alt statement without any active default.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot taken for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean guards.
requirements.original: This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot taken for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY include the top element of the port over which the procedure has been called, if any.
requirements.original: This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.

ambiguity.issue: 'may include' could mean the snapshot only contains the port top element if present, or that inclusion is optional for the tool; the reading 'includes it if present' is chosen.
readings: A snapshot for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL include the top element of the calling port if the queue is not empty.
A snapshot for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY optionally include the top element of the calling port.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot taken for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY include a timeout exception generated by the timer supervising the call, if such a timer is used.
requirements.original: This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.

requirements.original: Communication operation: Invoke procedure call; Keyword: call

requirements.canonical: The procedure-based communication operation "Accept procedure call from remote entity" IS denoted by the keyword `getcall`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Accept procedure call from remote entity; Keyword: getcall

requirements.original: Communication operation: Reply to procedure call from remote entity; Keyword: reply

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: The procedure-based communication operation "Raise exception (to an accepted call)" IS denoted by the keyword `raise`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Raise exception (to an accepted call); Keyword: raise

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The procedure-based communication operation "Handle response from a previous call" IS denoted by the keyword `getreply`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Handle response from a previous call; Keyword: getreply

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The procedure-based communication operation "Catch exception (from called entity)" IS denoted by the keyword `catch`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Catch exception (from called entity); Keyword: catch

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The procedure-based communication operation "Check call/exception/reply received" IS denoted by the keyword `check`.
requirements.original: Communication operation: Check call/exception/reply received; Keyword: check

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation MAY include a timeout value.
requirements.original: The call operation may optionally include a timeout.

requirements.subject: ent:call-timer-value
requirements.canonical: The timeout value of a `call` operation SHALL be an explicit value or constant of float type.
requirements.original: This is defined as an explicit value or constant of float type and defines the length of time after the call operation has started that a timeout exception shall be generated by the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.condition: a timeout value is present in the call operation
requirements.canonical: When a timeout value is given in a `call` operation, the test system SHALL generate a timeout exception when the given length of time has elapsed after the `call` operation has started.
requirements.original: This is defined as an explicit value or constant of float type and defines the length of time after the call operation has started that a timeout exception shall be generated by the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.condition: no timeout value is present in the call operation
requirements.canonical: If no timeout value part is present in a `call` operation, the test system SHALL NOT generate a timeout exception for the call.
requirements.original: If no timeout value part is present in the call operation, no timeout exception shall be generated.

requirements.subject: ent:nowait-keyword
requirements.condition: the nowait keyword is used
