requirements.canonical: When the keyword `nowait` is used instead of a timeout value in a `call` operation, the calling test component continues execution without waiting for a response, an exception raised by the called procedure, or a timeout exception.
requirements.original: Using the keyword nowait instead of a timeout exception value in a call operation allows calling a procedure to continue without waiting either for a response or an exception raised by the called procedure or a timeout exception.

requirements.subject: ent:port-queue
requirements.condition: the nowait keyword is used
requirements.canonical: If the `nowait` keyword is used in a `call` operation, a response or exception of the called procedure SHALL be removed from the port queue by a `getreply` or `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` statement.
requirements.original: If the nowait keyword is used, a possible response or exception of the called procedure has to be removed from the port queue by using a getreply or a catch operation in a subsequent alt statement.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether this is a requirement on the test writer (error if not removed) or a description of the only way to remove such entries; the description reading is chosen as primary.
readings: A response or exception to a `nowait` call can only be removed from the port queue by a `getreply` or `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` statement.
A test SHALL handle every response or exception of a `nowait` call in a subsequent `alt` statement, otherwise an error occurs.

requirements.subject: ent:blocking-procedure
requirements.canonical: A blocking procedure MAY have no return value, no out and inout parameters and raise no exception.
requirements.original: A blocking procedure may have no return values, no out and inout parameters and may raise no exception.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.condition: the called procedure is blocking and has no return value, out/inout parameters or exceptions
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation of a blocking procedure without return value, out parameters, inout parameters and exceptions SHALL have a response and exception handling part.
requirements.original: The call operation for such a procedure shall also have a response and exception handling part to handle the blocking in a uniform manner.

requirements.subject: ent:non-blocking-procedure
requirements.canonical: A non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT have out parameters, inout parameters or a return value.
requirements.original: A non-blocking procedure has no out and inout parameters, no return value and the non-blocking property is indicated in the corresponding signature definition by means of a noblock keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:noblock-keyword
requirements.canonical: The non-blocking property of a procedure IS indicated in its signature definition by the `noblock` keyword.
requirements.original: A non-blocking procedure has no out and inout parameters, no return value and the non-blocking property is indicated in the corresponding signature definition by means of a noblock keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure SHALL be removed from the port queue by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: Possible exceptions raised by non-blocking procedures have to be removed from the port queue by using catch operations in subsequent alt or interleave statements.

ambiguity.issue: Same as for nowait calls: obligation on the test writer vs. description of the only removal mechanism; obligation reading chosen.
readings: An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure SHALL be removed by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.
An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure CAN only be removed from the port queue by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation supports unicast, multicast and broadcast calls of procedures, like the `send` operation.
requirements.original: Like for the send operation, TTCN-3 also supports unicast, multicast and broadcast calls of procedures.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: For a unicast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS the address of one receiving entity.
requirements.original: This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: For a multicast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS a list of addresses of a set of receivers.
requirements.original: This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: For a broadcast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS the `all component` keyword.
requirements.original: This can be done in the same manner as described in clause 22.2.1, i.e. the argument of the to clause of a call operation is for unicast calls the address of one receiving entity (or can be omitted in case of one-to-one connections), for multicast calls a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast calls the all component keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.condition: one-to-one connection
requirements.canonical: In case of a one-to-one connection, the `to` clause of a `call` operation MAY be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.
requirements.original: In case of one-to-one connections, the to clause may be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: A multicast or broadcast `call` operation CAN cause several responses and exceptions from different communication partners.
requirements.original: A multicast or broadcast call operation may cause several responses and exceptions from different communication partners.

requirements.subject: ent:non-blocking-procedure
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a non-blocking procedure
requirements.canonical: For a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a non-blocking procedure, all exceptions raised by the different communication partners CAN be handled in subsequent `catch` operations, `alt` or `interleave` statements.
requirements.original: In case of a multicast or broadcast call operation of a non-blocking procedure, all exceptions which may be raised from the different communication partners can be handled in subsequent catch, alt or interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:response-and-exception-handling-part
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a blocking procedure
requirements.canonical: For a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a blocking procedure, the response and exception handling part of the `call` operation MAY handle only one response or exception.
requirements.original: In case of a multicast or broadcast call operation of a blocking procedure, responses and exceptions can be handled in several ways: one possibility is to handle only one response or exception in the response and exception handling part of the call operation.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: When only one response or exception of a multicast or broadcast blocking call is handled in the response and exception handling part, all further responses and exceptions ARE handled in subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statements.
requirements.original: All further responses and exceptions are handled in subsequent alt or interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:response-and-exception-handling-part
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a blocking procedure
requirements.canonical: For a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a blocking procedure, several or all responses and exceptions MAY be processed in the response and exception handling part by nested `alt` statements or by the `repeat` operation, which causes re-evaluation of the call body.
requirements.original: Alternatively, several or all responses and exceptions are processed in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of nested alt statements or by using the repeat operation causing the re-evaluation of the call body.

requirements.subject: ent:nowait-keyword
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a blocking procedure
requirements.canonical: For a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a blocking procedure, the `nowait` keyword MAY be used and all responses and exceptions handled in subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statements.
requirements.original: A further possibility is to use the nowait directive and to handle all responses and exceptions in subsequent alt or interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation SHALL only be used on procedure-based ports.
requirements.original: a) The call operation shall only be used on procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The port type definition of the port used in a `call` operation SHALL include the signature of the called procedure in its out or inout list.
requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the call operation belongs in its out or inout list i.e. it shall be allowed to call this procedure at this port.

ambiguity.issue: 'name of the procedure' is used where 'signature' is meant; 'out or inout list' refers to the out/inout direction lists of the port type.

requirements.subject: ent:in-parameter
requirements.canonical: All in and inout parameters of the signature used in a `call` operation SHALL have a specific value.
requirements.original: b) All in and inout parameters of the signature shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism such as AnyValue SHALL NOT be used for in and inout parameters of the signature in a `call` operation.
requirements.original: b) All in and inout parameters of the signature shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:out-parameter
requirements.canonical: In a `call` operation, only out parameters of the signature MAY be omitted or specified with a matching mechanism.
requirements.original: c) Only out parameters may be omitted or specified with a matching attribute.

ambiguity.issue: 'matching attribute' is used instead of 'matching mechanism'; 'omitted' refers to the not-used symbol '-'.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The signature arguments of a `call` operation ARE NOT used to retrieve variable names for out and inout parameters.
requirements.original: d) The signature arguments of the call operation are not used to retrieve variable names for out and inout parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:response-and-exception-handling-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment of the procedure return value and of out and inout parameter values to variables SHALL be made explicitly in the response and exception handling part of the `call` operation by `getreply` and `catch` operations.
requirements.original: The actual assignment of the procedure return value and out and inout parameter values to variables shall explicitly be made in the response and exception handling part of the call operation by means of getreply and catch operations.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: Signature templates MAY be used in `call` operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.
requirements.original: This allows the use of signature templates in call operations in the same manner as templates can be used for types.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.condition: one-to-many connection
requirements.canonical: A `to` clause SHALL be present in a `call` operation in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.original: e) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: Each AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `call` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `call` operation.
requirements.original: f) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the call operation.

ambiguity.issue: 'component' is used where 'a component type' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `call` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:call-timer-value
requirements.canonical: The CallTimerValue of a `call` operation SHALL be of type `float`.
requirements.original: g) CallTimerValue shall be of type float.

requirements.subject: ent:response-and-exception-handling-part
requirements.canonical: The selection of the alternatives of the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL only be based on `getreply` and `catch` operations for the called procedure.
requirements.original: h) The selection of the alternatives to a call shall only be based on getreply and catch operations for the called procedure.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: An unqualified `getreply` or `catch` operation in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL only treat replies from and exceptions raised by the called procedure.
requirements.original: Unqualified getreply and catch operations shall only treat replies from and exceptions raised by the called procedure.

ambiguity.issue: 'Unqualified' is not defined here; it may mean without a signature/from clause, or the any-port form. Chosen: operations without a signature-specific filter.
readings: A `getreply`/`catch` without signature reference in a call's handling part SHALL only treat replies/exceptions of the called procedure.
An `any port.getreply`/`any port.catch` in a call's handling part SHALL only treat replies/exceptions of the called procedure.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: An `else` branch SHALL NOT be used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation.
requirements.original: The use of else branches and the invocation of altsteps is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep SHALL NOT be invoked in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation.
requirements.original: The use of else branches and the invocation of altsteps is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of a Boolean guard in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation CAN have side effects.
requirements.original: i) The evaluation of the Boolean expressions guarding the alternatives in the response and exception handling part may have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: A Boolean guard in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL follow the same rules as Boolean guards in `alt` statements.
requirements.original: In order to avoid unexpected side effects, the same rules as for the Boolean guards in alt statements shall be applied (see clause 20.2).

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation for a blocking procedure without return value, out parameters, inout parameters and exceptions SHALL have a response and exception handling part.
requirements.original: j) The call operation for a blocking procedures without return value, out parameters, inout parameters and exceptions shall also have a response and exception handling part to handle the blocking in a uniform manner.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: multicast or broadcast call of a blocking procedure with nowait
requirements.canonical: In a multicast or broadcast `call` operation of a blocking procedure with the `nowait` keyword, all responses and exceptions SHALL be handled in subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statements.
requirements.original: k) In case of a multicast or broadcast call operation of a blocking procedure, where the nowait keyword is used, all responses and exceptions have to be handled in subsequent alt or interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.condition: the called procedure is non-blocking
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT have a response and exception handling part.
requirements.original: l) The call operation for a non-blocking procedure shall have no response and exception handling part, shall raise no timeout exception and shall not use the nowait keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.condition: the called procedure is non-blocking
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT raise a timeout exception.
requirements.original: l) The call operation for a non-blocking procedure shall have no response and exception handling part, shall raise no timeout exception and shall not use the nowait keyword.

ambiguity.issue: 'shall raise no timeout exception' likely means no CallTimerValue shall be given; chosen reading: no timeout value is allowed.
readings: A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT specify a CallTimerValue.
A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT generate a timeout exception at runtime even if a timer value is given.

requirements.subject: ent:nowait-keyword
requirements.condition: the called procedure is non-blocking
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT use the `nowait` keyword.
requirements.original: l) The call operation for a non-blocking procedure shall have no response and exception handling part, shall raise no timeout exception and shall not use the nowait keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-error
requirements.condition: the port is unmapped or disconnected
requirements.canonical: Applying a `call` operation to an unmapped or disconnected port SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: m) Applying a call operation to an unmapped or disconnected port shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `call` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: n) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation IS used to accept calls.
requirements.original: The getcall operation is used to accept calls.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `getcall` ["(" TemplateInstance ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`param` "(" parameter assignment list ")"] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]], where a parameter assignment is either a list of "ValueRef := [@decoded [(Expression)]] ParameterIdentifier" items or a positional list of ValueRef or "-" items.
requirements.original:
[ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." getcall
  [ "(" TemplateInstance ")" ] 
  [ from Address ]
  [ "->" [ param "(" { ( ValueRef":=" [ @decoded [ "(" Expression ")" ] ] 
          ParameterIdentifier ) "," } |
          { ( ValueRef| "-" ) "," } 
         ")" ]
     [ sender ValueRef] 
     [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `getcall` operation CAN be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation specifies that a test component accepts a call from the SUT or from another test component.
requirements.original: The getcall operation is used to specify that a test component accepts a call from the SUT, or another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.condition: the matching criteria associated to the getcall operation are fulfilled
requirements.canonical: If the matching criteria of a `getcall` operation are fulfilled, the `getcall` operation SHALL remove the top call from the incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The getcall operation shall remove the top call from the incoming port queue, if, and only if, the matching criteria associated to the getcall operation are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.condition: the matching criteria associated to the getcall operation are not fulfilled
requirements.canonical: If the matching criteria of a `getcall` operation are not fulfilled, the `getcall` operation SHALL NOT remove the top call from the incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The getcall operation shall remove the top call from the incoming port queue, if, and only if, the matching criteria associated to the getcall operation are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria of a `getcall` operation relate to the signature of the call to be processed and to the communication partner.
requirements.original: These matching criteria are related to the signature of the call to be processed and the communication partner.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria for the signature of a `getcall` operation MAY be specified in-line or be derived from a signature template.
requirements.original: The matching criteria for the signature may either be specified in-line or be derived from a signature template.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment of `in` and `inout` parameter values to variables SHALL be made in the assignment part of the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: The assignment of in and inout parameter values to variables shall be made in the assignment part of the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: Keeping parameter assignment in the assignment part allows signature templates to be used in `getcall` operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.
requirements.original: This allows the use of signature templates in getcall operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.condition: one-to-many connection
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-many connections, a `getcall` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: A getcall operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The restriction of a `getcall` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted by the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted by using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:one-to-one-connection
requirements.canonical: A one-to-one connection IS a simple case of a one-to-many connection, and a `getcall` operation on a one-to-one connection MAY use the `from` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The optional assignment part of the `getcall` operation comprises the assignment of `in` and `inout` parameter values to variables and the retrieval of the address of the calling component.
requirements.original: The (optional) assignment part of the getcall operation comprises the assignment of in and inout parameter values to variables and the retrieval of the address of the calling component.

requirements.subject: ent:param-clause
requirements.canonical: The `param` keyword IS used to retrieve the parameter values of a call accepted by a `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: The keyword param is used to retrieve the parameter values of a call.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: When assigning individual parameters of a call in a `getcall` operation, encoded parameters MAY be decoded prior to assignment using the `@decoded` modifier.
requirements.original: When assigning individual parameters of a call, encoded parameters can be decoded prior to assignment using the @decoded modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used
requirements.canonical: If the `@decoded` modifier is used in a `param` clause, the referenced parameter on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring type.
requirements.original: In this case, the referenced parameter on the right hand sided of the assignment shall be one of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal `charstring types.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used
requirements.canonical: A parameter assigned with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: It shall be` decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: decoding fails
requirements.canonical: Failure of the decoding of a parameter assigned with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the referenced parameter is of the universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the referenced parameter is of the universal charstring type, the `@decoded` clause MAY contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.original: In case the referenced field is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded` clause can contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.

ambiguity.issue: The text speaks of a 'referenced field', but in a getcall param clause the referenced item is a signature parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL be of the charstring type.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause that is not one of the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: The kind of error is not stated; the most likely reading is a test case error at runtime (the value may be non-constant), but a compile-time error is required when the value is known statically.
readings: An encoding format parameter value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
An encoding format parameter value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a compile-time error if it can be determined statically.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the referenced parameter is not of the universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the referenced parameter is not of the universal charstring type, the encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.original: In case the referenced field is not a universal **charstring, the optional** parameter shall not be present.

ambiguity.issue: The text speaks of a 'referenced field', but in a getcall param clause the referenced item is a signature parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: The `sender` keyword IS used to retrieve the address of the sender of a call accepted by a `getcall` operation, e.g. for addressing a reply or exception to the calling party in a one-to-many configuration.
requirements.original: The keyword sender is used when it is required to retrieve the address of the sender (e.g. for addressing a reply or exception to the calling party in a one-to-many configuration).

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.condition: no signature argument list is given
requirements.canonical: A `getcall` operation without an argument list for the signature matching criteria removes the call on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.
requirements.original: A getcall operation with no argument list for the signature matching criteria will remove the call on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: A `getcall` on any port IS denoted by the `any` keyword (`any port.getcall`).
requirements.original: To getcall on any port is denoted by the any keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from
requirements.canonical: A `getcall` on any port from a specific port array IS denoted by the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.
requirements.original: To getcall on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array-ref
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` `getcall` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To getcall on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: For a single-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the `getcall` operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type integer.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a singledimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the `getcall` operation was successful MAY be stored in an integer array or record of integer variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a singledimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from
requirements.canonical: When an `any from` `getcall` operation checks the port array for matching calls, the iteration over the port indices IS from lowest to highest index.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching calls, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the ports checked by an `any from` `getcall` operation are iterated from innermost to outermost array dimension, from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

requirements.subject: ent:any-from
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all criteria causes the `any from` `getcall` operation to be successful, even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation SHALL only be used on procedure-based ports.
requirements.original: a) The getcall operation shall only be used on procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port used in a `getcall` operation SHALL include the signature to which the `getcall` operation belongs in its `in` or `inout` list.
requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the getcall operation belongs in its in or inout list.

ambiguity.issue: 'procedure' is used where the signature (procedure signature) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The signature argument of the `getcall` operation SHALL NOT be used to pass in variable names for `in` and `inout` parameters.
requirements.original: b) The signature argument of the getcall operation shall not be used to pass in variable names for in and inout parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:parameter-identifier
requirements.canonical: The ParameterIdentifiers in the `param` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be from the corresponding signature definition.
requirements.original: c) The ParameterIdentifiers shall be from the corresponding signature definition.

requirements.subject: ent:value-assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The value assignment part (`-> value`) SHALL NOT be used with the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: d) The value assignment part shall not be used with the getcall operation.

ambiguity.issue: 'value assignment part' is not defined for getcall; the syntax permits '@index value', so it is unclear what is forbidden. Chosen reading: the value redirect '-> value' known from receive operations.
readings: A value redirect (`-> value VariableRef`) SHALL NOT be used with the `getcall` operation.
No assignment using the `value` keyword (including `@index value`) SHALL be used with the `getcall` operation.

requirements.subject: ent:param-clause
requirements.condition: the getcall operation accepts any call
requirements.canonical: A `getcall` operation without a signature argument (accepting any call) SHALL NOT contain a `param` clause.
requirements.original: e) Parameters of calls accepted by accepting any call shall not be assigned to a variable, i.e. the param clause shall not be present.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `from` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: f) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef item in the `sender` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: f) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array-ref
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef of a `getcall` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: g) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection (`@index value`) SHALL only be used when the `getcall` operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: h) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the port array.
requirements.original: i) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional port arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the same as the dimension of the port array.
requirements.original: j) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.original: j) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-or-fuzzy-variable
requirements.condition: the redirect variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `param`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `getcall` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to that variable IS equal to the result produced by the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: k) If a variable referenced in the param, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the getcall operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-or-fuzzy-variable
requirements.condition: the redirect variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: Later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `param`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `getcall` operation does NOT lead to repeated invocation of the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: k) If a variable referenced in the param, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the getcall operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: both from and sender clause are present
requirements.canonical: If the `getcall` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the template in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: l) If the getcall operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: sender clause present, from clause absent
requirements.canonical: If the `getcall` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the type of the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the type of the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.

ambiguity.issue: 'the sender' could denote the statically known address type of the port/connection or the actual runtime sender; NOTE 3 suggests a check where the sender type can be determined.
readings: If no `from` clause is present, the type of the sender, where it can be determined statically, SHALL be type compatible with the type of the `sender` clause variable (compile-time check).
If no `from` clause is present, the actual sender address at runtime SHALL be type compatible with the type of the `sender` clause variable, otherwise an error occurs.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: An error due to a type mismatch CAN occur if the types in the signature matching part of a `getcall` operation are not compatible to the types in the assignment part, or if the `from` clause is missing and the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

ambiguity.issue: NOTE 3 uses 'receive part' in the getcall clause, where the signature matching part (TemplateInstance) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:decmatch
requirements.condition: @decoded used together with decmatch matching for the parameter
requirements.canonical: When assigning a parameter decoded with `@decoded` whose matching template uses MatchDecodedContent (`decmatch`) matching, the type of the template in the `decmatch` matching SHALL be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded parameter is stored into.
requirements.original: m) When assigning implicitly decoded parameters (by using the @decoded modifier) in cases where the value or template to be matched uses the MatchDecodedContent (decmatch) matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the MatchDecodedContent matching shall be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `getcall` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: n) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `getcall` statements.
requirements.original: o) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone getcall statements.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `reply` operation IS used to reply to a call.
requirements.original: The reply operation is used to reply to a call.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `reply` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `reply` "(" TemplateInstance [`value` TemplateBody] ")" [`to` Address].
requirements.original:
ObjectReference "." reply "(" TemplateInstance [ value TemplateBody ] ")" 
  [ to Address ]

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `to` clause of a `reply` operation CAN be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `all component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `reply` operation replies to a previously accepted call according to the procedure signature.
requirements.original: The reply operation is used to reply to a previously accepted call according to the procedure signature.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: The relation between an accepted call and a `reply` operation CANNOT always be checked statically.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The relation between an accepted call and a reply operation cannot always be checked statically.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: A `reply` operation MAY be specified without an associated `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: For testing it is allowed to specify a reply operation without an associated getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: The value part of the `reply` operation consists of a signature reference with an associated actual parameter list and an optional return value.
requirements.original: The value part of the reply operation consists of a signature reference with an associated actual parameter list and (optional) return value.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: The signature in a `reply` operation MAY be defined in the form of a signature template or in-line.
requirements.original: The signature may either be defined in the form of a signature template or it may be defined in-line.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: Responses to one or more call operations MAY be sent to one, several or all peer entities connected to the addressed port.
requirements.original: Responses to one or more call operations may be sent to one, several or all peer entities connected to the addressed port.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: For a unicast response, the argument of the `to` clause of a `reply` operation IS the address of one receiving entity.
requirements.original: This means, the argument of the to clause of a reply operation is for unicast responses the address of one receiving entity, for multicast responses a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast responses the all component keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: For a multicast response, the argument of the `to` clause of a `reply` operation IS a list of addresses of a set of receivers.
requirements.original: This means, the argument of the to clause of a reply operation is for unicast responses the address of one receiving entity, for multicast responses a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast responses the all component keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: For a broadcast response, the argument of the `to` clause of a `reply` operation IS the `all component` keywords.
requirements.original: This means, the argument of the to clause of a reply operation is for unicast responses the address of one receiving entity, for multicast responses a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast responses the all component keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.condition: one-to-one connection
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-one connections, the `to` clause of a `reply` operation MAY be omitted.
requirements.original: In case of one-to-one connections, the to clause may be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.

requirements.subject: ent:return-value
requirements.canonical: A return value or template of a `reply` operation SHALL be explicitly stated with the `value` keyword.
requirements.original: A return value or template shall be explicitly stated with the value keyword and is first evaluated before returning.

requirements.subject: ent:return-value
requirements.canonical: A return value or template of a `reply` operation IS evaluated before returning.
requirements.original: A return value or template shall be explicitly stated with the value keyword and is first evaluated before returning.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: A `reply` operation SHALL only be used at a procedure-based port.
requirements.original: a) A reply operation shall only be used at a procedure-based port.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port used in a `reply` operation SHALL include the signature to which the `reply` operation belongs in its `in` or `inout` list.
requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the reply operation belongs in its in or inout list.

ambiguity.issue: 'procedure' is used where the signature (procedure signature) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance in the `reply` operation SHALL identify the signature definition and all signature parameters of the signature to which the `reply` operation belongs.
requirements.original: b) The TemplateInstance in the reply operation shall identify the signature definition and all signature parameters of the procedure to which the reply operation belongs.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: All `out` and `inout` parameters of the signature in a `reply` operation SHALL have a specific value, i.e. matching mechanisms such as AnyValue SHALL NOT be used for them.
requirements.original: c) All out and inout parameters of the signature shall have a specific value i.e. the use of matching mechanisms such as AnyValue is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.condition: one-to-many connection
requirements.canonical: A `to` clause SHALL be present in a `reply` operation in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.original: d) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `to` clause of a `reply` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `reply` operation.
requirements.original: e) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the reply operation.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `reply` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:value-clause
requirements.canonical: The optional `value` clause of a `reply` operation SHALL only be present if the signature definition to which the `reply` operation belongs defines a return type.
requirements.original: f) The optional value clause for a return value shall only be present if the signature definition of the procedure to which the reply operation belongs defines a return type.

requirements.subject: ent:value-clause
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody in the `value` clause of a `reply` operation SHALL conform to the template(value) restriction.
requirements.original: g) The TemplateBody in the value clause shall conform to the template(value) restriction and it shall be type-compatible with the return type specified in the signature of the procedure to which the reply operation belongs.

requirements.subject: ent:value-clause
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody in the `value` clause of a `reply` operation SHALL be type-compatible with the return type specified in the signature to which the `reply` operation belongs.
requirements.original: g) The TemplateBody in the value clause shall conform to the template(value) restriction and it shall be type-compatible with the return type specified in the signature of the procedure to which the reply operation belongs.

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.condition: the port is unmapped or disconnected
requirements.canonical: Applying a `reply` operation to an unmapped or disconnected port SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: h) Applying a reply operation to an unmapped or disconnected port shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `reply` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: i) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getreply` operation IS used to handle replies from a previously called procedure.
requirements.original: The getreply operation is used to handle replies from a previously called procedure.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getreply` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `getreply` ["(" TemplateInstance [`value` TemplateInstance] ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`value` (ValueRef | "(" {ValueRef [":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] FieldOrTypeReference] [","]} ")")] [`param` "(" ({ValueRef ":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] ParameterIdentifier ","} | {(ValueRef | "-") ","}) ")"] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index` `value` ValueRef]].
requirements.original: [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." getreply [ "(" TemplateInstance [ value TemplateInstance ]")" ] [ from Address ] [ "->" [ value ... ] [ param ... ] [ sender ValueRef] [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `getreply` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getreply` operation SHALL remove the top reply from the incoming port queue if, and only if, the matching criteria associated with the `getreply` operation are fulfilled.
requirements.original: The getreply operation shall remove the top reply from the incoming port queue, if, and only if, the matching criteria associated to the getreply operation are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria of a `getreply` operation ARE related to the signature of the procedure to be processed and to the communication partner.
requirements.original: These matching criteria are related to the signature of the procedure to be processed and the communication partner.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The signature matching criteria of a `getreply` operation MAY be specified in-line or be derived from a signature template.
requirements.original: The matching criteria for the signature may either be specified in-line or be derived from a signature template.

requirements.subject: ent:value-keyword
requirements.canonical: Matching against a received return value in a `getreply` operation MAY be specified by using the `value` keyword.
requirements.original: Matching against a received return value can be specified by using the value keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.condition: one-to-many connections
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-many connections, a `getreply` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: A getreply operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: A restriction of a `getreply` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted by the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted by using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: For one-to-one connections, which are a simple case of one-to-many connections, the `from` clause MAY be used in a `getreply` operation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment of out and inout parameter values to variables SHALL be made in the assignment part of the `getreply` operation.
requirements.original: The assignment of out and inout parameter values to variables shall be made in the assignment part of the getreply operation.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: Making out and inout parameter assignments in the assignment part ALLOWS signature templates to be used in `getreply` operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.
requirements.original: This allows the use of signature templates in getreply operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The optional assignment part of the `getreply` operation IS composed of the assignment of out and inout parameter values to variables and the retrieval of the address of the sender of the reply.
requirements.original: The (optional) assignment part of the getreply operation comprises the assignment of out and inout parameter values to variables and the retrieval of the address of the sender of the reply.

requirements.subject: ent:value-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `value` keyword in the assignment part of a `getreply` operation IS used to retrieve the return value of a reply.
requirements.original: The keyword value is used to retrieve return values and the keyword param is used to retrieve the parameter values of a reply.

requirements.subject: ent:param-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `param` keyword in the assignment part of a `getreply` operation IS used to retrieve the parameter values of a reply.
requirements.original: The keyword value is used to retrieve return values and the keyword param is used to retrieve the parameter values of a reply.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `sender` keyword in the assignment part of a `getreply` operation IS used to retrieve the address of the sender of the reply.
requirements.original: The keyword sender is used when it is required to retrieve the address of the sender.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: When individual parameters or referenced fields of the return value of a reply are assigned, encoded parameters MAY be decoded prior to assignment by using the `@decoded` modifier.
requirements.original: When assigning individual parameters or referenced fields of the return value of a reply, encoded parameters can be decoded prior to assignment using the @decoded modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used
requirements.canonical: If the `@decoded` modifier is used, the referenced parameter or field of the return value on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be of a bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring type.
requirements.original: In this case, the referenced parameter or field of the return value on the right hand sided of the assignment shall be one of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used
requirements.canonical: If the `@decoded` modifier is used, the referenced parameter or field SHALL be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: It shall be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: A failure of the decoding of a parameter or field with the `@decoded` modifier in a `getreply` operation SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the parameter or field is of universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the parameter or referenced field of the return value is of the universal charstring type, the `@decoded` clause MAY contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.original: In case the parameter or referenced field of the return value is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded clause can contain an` optional parameter defining the encoding format.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL be of the charstring type.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.

readings: An invalid encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
An invalid encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause SHALL cause a compile-time error when it is statically known.
ambiguity.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or test case error) is not stated; the canonical keeps the generic 'error'.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the parameter or field is not of universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the parameter or referenced field of the return value is not of the universal charstring type, the optional encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.original: In case the parameter or referenced field of the return value is not a universal **char string, the** optional parameter shall not be present.

ambiguity.issue: The text writes 'universal char string' (PDF formatting artefact) where the type 'universal charstring' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:get-any-reply
requirements.canonical: A `getreply` operation with no argument list for the signature matching criteria SHALL remove the reply on the top of the incoming port queue, if any, if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.
requirements.original: A getreply operation with no argument list for the signature matching criteria shall remove the reply message on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:get-any-reply
requirements.condition: used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation
requirements.canonical: If a get any reply operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation, it SHALL only treat replies from the procedure invoked by that `call` operation.
requirements.original: If GetAnyReply is used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation, it shall only treat replies from the procedure invoked by the call operation.

improper_terms.proper: get any reply (getreply operation without signature argument)

ambiguity.issue: 'GetAnyReply' is a BNF-style name that is not defined in this clause; the 'get any reply' form of the getreply operation is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: A `getreply` operation on any port IS specified by using the `any port` keywords.
requirements.original: To get a reply on any port, use the any port keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: A `getreply` operation on any port of a specific port array IS specified by using the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.
requirements.original: To get a reply on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` PortArrayRef construct of a `getreply` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To get a reply on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index of the port of a single-dimensional port array at which the `getreply` operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type integer.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the `getreply` operation was successful MAY be stored in an integer array or record of integer variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: When a port array is checked for matching replies, the port indices to be checked ARE iterated from lowest to highest.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching replies, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.condition: the port array is multi-dimensional
requirements.canonical: If the port array is multi-dimensional, the ports ARE iterated over from the innermost to the outermost array dimension, from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

readings: The last index varies fastest, as shown by the example sequence [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The innermost dimension (first index) is iterated over first, i.e. the first index varies fastest.
ambiguity.issue: 'From innermost to outermost' could be read as the first index varying fastest, but the example sequence shows the last index varying fastest; the canonical follows the example.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all the criteria CAUSES the `getreply` operation to be successful, even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: A `getreply` operation SHALL only be used at a procedure-based port.
requirements.original: a) A getreply operation shall only be used at a procedure-based port.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port at which a `getreply` operation is used SHALL include the name of the procedure (signature) to which the `getreply` operation belongs.
requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the getreply operation belongs.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The signature argument of a `getreply` operation SHALL NOT be used to pass in variable names for out and inout parameters.
requirements.original: b) The signature argument of the getreply operation shall not be used to pass in variable names for out and inout parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:get-any-reply
requirements.canonical: Parameters or return values of replies accepted by a get any reply operation SHALL NOT be assigned to a variable, i.e. the `param` and `value` clauses SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.original: c) Parameters or return values of responses accepted by get any reply shall not be assigned to a variable, i.e. the **param and value clause shall not be present.**

ambiguity.issue: 'responses' is used where 'replies' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: All AddressRef items in the `from` clause and all ValueRef items in the `sender` clause of a `getreply` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `getreply` operation.
requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the getreply operation.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `getreply` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef of a `getreply` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: e) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of a `getreply` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.
requirements.original: g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the respective port array.
requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

ambiguity.issue: 'the dimension of the respective port array' means the number of dimensions of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `value`, `param`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `getreply` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to that variable IS equal to the result produced by the `getreply` operation, and later evaluation of the variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the `getreply` operation.
requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the value, param, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the getreply operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the getreply operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: the getreply operation contains both from and sender clause
requirements.canonical: If a `getreply` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the template in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: j) If the getreply operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: the getreply operation contains a sender clause but no from clause
requirements.canonical: If a `getreply` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: An error due to a type mismatch MAY occur if the types in the receive part of a `getreply` operation are not compatible with the types in the assignment part, or if the `from` clause is missing and the determinable type of the sender is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:decmatch
requirements.condition: @decoded is used and the matched template uses decmatch for that parameter
requirements.canonical: When implicitly decoded parameters or referenced fields of the return value are assigned by using the `@decoded` modifier and the value or template to be matched uses `decmatch` matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the `decmatch` matching SHALL be type compatible with the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.
requirements.original: k) When assigning implicitly decoded parameters or referenced fields of the return value (by using the @decoded modifier) in cases where the value or template to be matched uses the MatchDecodedContent (decmatch) matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the MatchDecodedContent matching shall be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `getreply` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: l) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `getreply` statements.
requirements.original: m) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone getreply statements.

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: An exception IS raised with the `raise` operation.
requirements.original: Exceptions are raised with the raise operation.

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
