requirements.canonical: The `raise` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `raise` "(" Signature "," TemplateInstance ")" [`to` Address].
requirements.original: ObjectReference "." raise "(" Signature "," TemplateInstance ")" [ to Address ]

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `to` clause of a `raise` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `all component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: The `raise` operation IS used to raise an exception.
requirements.original: The raise operation is used to raise an exception.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool CANNOT always check statically the relation between an accepted call and a `raise` operation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The relation between an accepted call and a raise operation cannot always be checked statically.

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: For testing, a `raise` operation MAY be specified without an associated `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: For testing it is allowed to specify a raise operation without an associated getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: The value part of the `raise` operation IS composed of the signature reference followed by the exception value.
requirements.original: The value part of the raise operation consists of the signature reference followed by the exception value.

requirements.subject: ent:exception
requirements.canonical: An exception IS specified as a type.
requirements.original: Exceptions are specified as types.

requirements.subject: ent:exception-value
requirements.canonical: The exception value of a `raise` operation MAY be derived from a template conforming to the template(value) restriction or be the value resulting from an expression.
requirements.original: Therefore the exception value may either be derived from a template conforming to the template(value) restriction or be the value resulting from an expression (which of course can be an explicit value).

requirements.subject: ent:exception-value
requirements.condition: the type of the value being sent is ambiguous
requirements.canonical: If it is necessary to avoid ambiguity of the type of the value being sent, the optional type field in the value specification of the `raise` operation SHALL be used.
requirements.original: The optional type field in the value specification to the raise operation shall be used in cases where it is necessary to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being sent.

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: An exception to one or more `call` operations MAY be sent to one, several or all peer entities connected to the addressed port.
requirements.original: Exceptions to one or more call operations may be sent to one, several or all peer entities connected to the addressed port.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.canonical: The argument of the `to` clause of a `raise` operation IS the address of one receiving entity for unicast exceptions, a list of addresses of a set of receivers for multicast exceptions, and the `all component` keywords for broadcast exceptions.
requirements.original: This means, the argument of the to clause of a raise operation is for unicast exceptions the address of one receiving entity, for multicast exceptions a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast exceptions the all component keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.condition: one-to-one connection
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-one connections, the `to` clause of a `raise` operation MAY be omitted.
requirements.original: In case of one-to-one connections, the to clause may be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: An exception SHALL only be raised at a procedure-based port.
requirements.original: a) An exception shall only be raised at a procedure-based port.

requirements.subject: ent:exception
requirements.canonical: An exception IS a reaction to an accepted procedure call the result of which leads to an exceptional event.
requirements.original: An exception is a reaction to an accepted procedure call the result of which leads to an exceptional event.

requirements.subject: ent:exception
requirements.canonical: The type of the exception raised by a `raise` operation SHALL be specified in the signature of the called procedure.
requirements.original: b) The type of the exception shall be specified in the signature of the called procedure.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port at which a `raise` operation is used SHALL include in its `in` or `inout` list the name of the procedure (signature) to which the exception belongs.
requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include in its in or inout list the name of the procedure to which the exception belongs.

requirements.subject: ent:to-clause
requirements.condition: one-to-many connections
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-many connections, a `to` clause SHALL be present in a `raise` operation.
requirements.original: c) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: All AddressRef items in the `to` clause of a `raise` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `raise` operation.
requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the raise operation.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `raise` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: Applying a `raise` operation to an unmapped or disconnected port SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: e) Applying a raise operation to an unmapped or disconnected port shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `raise` operation SHALL conform to the template(value) restriction.
requirements.original: f) The TemplateInstance shall conform to the template(value) restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `raise` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: g) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The `catch` operation IS used to catch exceptions.
requirements.original: The catch operation is used to catch exceptions.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The `catch` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `catch` ["(" (Signature ["," TemplateInstance]) | `timeout` ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`value` (ValueRef | "(" {ValueRef [":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] FieldOrTypeReference] [","]} ")")] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]].
requirements.original: [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." catch [ "(" ( Signature [ "," TemplateInstance ] ) | TimeoutKeyword ")" ] [ from Address ] [ "->" [ value ( ValueRef| ( "(" { ValueRef[ ":=" [ @decoded [ "(" Expression ")" ] ] FieldOrTypeReference ][","] } ")" ) ) ] [ sender ValueRef] [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `catch` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The `catch` operation IS used to catch exceptions raised by a test component or the SUT as a reaction to a procedure call.
requirements.original: The catch operation is used to catch exceptions raised by a test component or the SUT as a reaction to a procedure call.

requirements.subject: ent:exception
requirements.canonical: An exception IS specified as a type and CAN be treated like a message.
requirements.original: Exceptions are specified as types and thus, can be treated like messages, e.g. templates can be used to distinguish between different values of the same exception type.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template MAY be used in a `catch` operation to distinguish between different values of the same exception type.
requirements.original: Exceptions are specified as types and thus, can be treated like messages, e.g. templates can be used to distinguish between different values of the same exception type.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.condition: a Signature is given in the parameter list
requirements.canonical: If a Signature is given in the parameter list of a `catch` operation, the TemplateInstance MAY be omitted, in which case the `catch` operation matches any exception value of any of the exception types declared in the definition of the referenced signature.
requirements.original: If a Signature is given in the parameter list, it is possible to omit the TemplateInstance part if the catch operation shall match any exception value of any of the exception types declared in the definition of the referenced Signature.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The `catch` operation removes the top exception from the associated incoming port queue if, and only if, that top exception satisfies all the matching criteria associated with the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: The catch operation removes the top exception from the associated incoming port queue if, and only if, that top exception satisfies all the matching criteria associated with the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.condition: one-to-many connections
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-many connections, a `catch` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: A catch operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: A restriction of a `catch` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted by the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted by using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: A `from` clause MAY be used in a `catch` operation on a one-to-one connection, which is considered a simple case of a one-to-many connection.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:redirection-part
requirements.canonical: The optional redirection part of a `catch` operation IS the storing of the exception value and/or one or more of its parts and the retrieval of the address of the component that raised the exception.
requirements.original: The (optional) redirection part of the catch operation comprises of storing the exception value and/or one or more parts of it and the retrieval of the address of the calling component.

improper_terms.proper: sender (the component that raised the exception)

ambiguity.issue: The exception is raised by the called component; 'calling component' is misleading. The `sender` clause retrieves the address of the component that raised the exception, as stated in the next sentence.

requirements.subject: ent:value-clause
requirements.canonical: The `value` keyword in the redirection part of a `catch` operation IS used to retrieve the value of an exception and/or parts of it.
requirements.original: The keyword value is used to retrieve the value of an exception and/or the parts of it and the keyword sender is used when it is required to retrieve the address of the sender.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: The `sender` keyword in the redirection part of a `catch` operation IS used to retrieve the address of the sender of the exception.
requirements.original: The keyword value is used to retrieve the value of an exception and/or the parts of it and the keyword sender is used when it is required to retrieve the address of the sender.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: When individual fields of an exception are assigned in the redirection part of a `catch` operation, encoded payload fields MAY be decoded prior to assignment using the `@decoded` modifier.
requirements.original: When assigning individual fields of an exception, encoded payload fields can be decoded prior to assignment using the @decoded modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used
requirements.canonical: If the `@decoded` modifier is used in a `catch` value redirect, the referenced field on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be of a `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring` or `universal charstring` type.
requirements.original: In this case, the referenced field on the right hand sided of the assignment shall be one of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: A field redirected with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: It shall be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: A failure of the decoding of a field redirected with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the referenced field is of the universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the referenced field is of the `universal charstring` type, the `@decoded` clause MAY contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.original: In case the referenced field is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded` clause can contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL be of the `charstring` type.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.

readings: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a compile-time error if it is known at compile time and a runtime error otherwise.
An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
ambiguity.issue: The kind of error (static or dynamic) is not specified; the canonical text keeps the generic 'error'.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the referenced field is not a universal charstring
requirements.canonical: If the referenced field is not of the `universal charstring` type, the encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.original: In case the referenced field is not a universal **charstring, the optional** parameter shall not be present.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation MAY be part of the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation.
requirements.original: The catch operation may be part of the response and exception handling part of a call operation or be used to determine an alternative in an alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation MAY be used to determine an alternative in an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The catch operation may be part of the response and exception handling part of a call operation or be used to determine an alternative in an alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: If a `catch` operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation, the port name and signature reference IS redundant information, because it follows from the `call` operation.
requirements.original: If the catch operation is used in the accepting part of a call operation, the information about port name and signature reference to indicate the procedure that raised the exception is redundant, because this information follows from the call operation.

ambiguity.issue: The call operation part is called 'response and exception handling part' elsewhere in the clause.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.condition: the catch operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation
requirements.canonical: If a `catch` operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation, the port name and signature reference SHALL nevertheless be given.
requirements.original: However, for readability reasons (e.g. in case of complex call statements) this information shall be repeated.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-exception
requirements.canonical: The timeout exception IS a special exception that CAN be caught by the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: There is one special timeout exception that can be caught by the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-exception
requirements.canonical: The timeout exception IS raised when a called procedure neither replies nor raises an exception within the predetermined time given in the `call` operation.
requirements.original: The timeout exception is an emergency exit for cases where a called procedure neither replies nor raises an exception within a predetermined time (see clause 22.3.1).

requirements.subject: ent:catch-any-exception
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation with no argument list catches any valid exception.
requirements.original: A catch operation with no argument list allows any valid exception to be caught.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-any-exception
requirements.canonical: The most general form of catch any exception IS a `catch` operation without argument list and without `from` clause.
requirements.original: The most general case is without using the from keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-any-exception
requirements.canonical: A catch any exception operation also catches the timeout exception.
requirements.original: CatchAnyException will also catch the timeout exception.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation with only a Signature reference in the argument list catches any valid exception of that signature.
requirements.original: A catch operation using only a Signature reference in the argument list allows any valid exception for that signature to be caught.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation on any port IS written with the `any port` keywords.
requirements.original: To catch an exception on any port use the any keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation on any port of a specific port array IS written with the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.
requirements.original: To catch an exception on any port from a specific port array, indices use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` `catch` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To catch an exception on any port from a specific port array, indices use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: In an `any from` `catch` operation on a single-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type `integer`.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: In an `any from` `catch` operation on a multi-dimensional port array, the index of the successful port MAY be stored in an integer array or `record of integer` variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: When an `any from` `catch` operation checks a port array for matching exceptions, the port indices IS iterated from lowest to highest.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching exceptions, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.condition: the port array is multi-dimensional
requirements.canonical: When an `any from` `catch` operation checks a multi-dimensional port array, the ports IS iterated from innermost to outermost array dimension and from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The first port in iteration order that matches all the criteria makes an `any from` `catch` operation successful, even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation on any port from a port array SHALL NOT be used to catch a call timeout.
requirements.original: The catch on any port from a port array operation cannot be used to catch a call timeout.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The `catch` operation SHALL only be used at procedure-based ports.
requirements.original: a) The catch operation shall only be used at procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:exception
requirements.canonical: The type of an exception caught by a `catch` operation SHALL be specified in the signature of the procedure that raised the exception.
requirements.original: The type of the caught exception shall be specified in the signature of the procedure that raised the exception.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port used in a `catch` operation SHALL include in its `out` or `inout` list the signature to which the caught exception belongs.
requirements.original: b) The type definition of the port shall include in its out or inout list the name of the procedure to which the exception belongs.

ambiguity.issue: Port type lists contain signature references; 'procedure' is used loosely for the signature.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation SHALL NOT bind incoming values to the terms of the expression or to the template.
requirements.original: c) No binding of the incoming values to the terms of the expression or to the template shall occur.

requirements.subject: ent:redirection-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment of exception values to variables SHALL be made in the redirection (assignment) part of the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: The assignment of the exception values to variables shall be made in the assignment part of the catch operation.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax and the semantic description call this the redirection part.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-exception
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation for the timeout exception SHALL only be used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation.
requirements.original: d) Catching timeout exceptions shall be restricted to the exception handling part of a call.

improper_terms.used: exception handling part of a call
improper_terms.proper: response and exception handling part of a call operation

ambiguity.issue: Elsewhere the clause uses 'response and exception handling part'.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-exception
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation that handles the timeout exception SHALL NOT contain further matching criteria, including a `from` clause.
requirements.original: No further matching criteria (including a from part) and no assignment part is allowed for a catch operation that handles a timeout exception.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-exception
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation that handles the timeout exception SHALL NOT contain a redirection (assignment) part.
requirements.original: No further matching criteria (including a from part) and no assignment part is allowed for a catch operation that handles a timeout exception.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-any-exception
requirements.canonical: A catch any exception operation SHALL NOT contain a `value` clause, i.e. accepted exception values SHALL NOT be assigned to a variable.
requirements.original: e) Exception values accepted by catch any exception shall not be assigned to a variable, i.e. the value clause shall not be present.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-any-exception
requirements.condition: CatchAnyException is used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation
requirements.canonical: If a catch any exception operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation, it SHALL only treat exceptions raised by the procedure invoked by that `call` operation.
requirements.original: f) If CatchAnyException is used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation, it shall only treat exceptions raised by the procedure invoked by the call operation.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `catch` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: g) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef in the `sender` clause of a `catch` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: g) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `catch` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` `catch` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: h) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection (`@index value`) in a `catch` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: i) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for single-dimensional arrays
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.
requirements.original: j) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or `record of integer` variable SHALL be exactly the same as the dimension of the respective port array.
requirements.original: k) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or `record of integer` variable SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.original: k) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `value`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `catch` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to that variable IS equal to the result produced by the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: l) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the catch operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: A later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable assigned in the redirection part of a `catch` operation IS NOT a repeated invocation of the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: l) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the catch operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: the catch operation contains both from and sender clause
requirements.canonical: If a `catch` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the template in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: m) If the catch operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause
requirements.canonical: If a `catch` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the types in the receive part are not compatible with the types in the assignment part, or, if the `from` clause is missing, if the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

improper_terms.proper: matching part (signature and template instance) of the catch operation

ambiguity.issue: The note is copied from the receive operation; for catch the 'receive part' is the exception matching part.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used and the matched field uses decmatch
requirements.canonical: When an exception field is assigned with the `@decoded` modifier and the value or template to be matched uses MatchDecodedContent (`decmatch`) matching for that field, the type of the template in the `decmatch` matching SHALL be type compatible with the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.
requirements.original: n) When assigning implicitly decoded exception fields (by using the @decoded modifier) in cases where the value or template to be matched uses the MatchDecodedContent (decmatch) matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the MatchDecodedContent matching shall be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The value referenced by the ObjectReference before the `catch` keyword, or the return type of a function instance used there, SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: o) The referenced value associated with Ref or the return type associated with FunctionInstance followed by the catch keyword, shall be of a port type.

ambiguity.issue: The syntactical structure of the catch operation uses ObjectReference; Ref and FunctionInstance do not appear in it.

requirements.subject: ent:value-clause
requirements.condition: no TemplateInstance is provided in the parameter list
requirements.canonical: If no TemplateInstance is provided in the parameter list of a `catch` operation, the redirection part SHALL NOT contain a `value` clause.
requirements.original: p) If no TemplateInstance is provided in the parameter list, then also no value clause shall be present in the redirection part.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `catch` statements.
requirements.original: q) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone catch statements.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation IS an operation that reads the top element of a message-based or procedure-based incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The check operation allows reading the top element of a message-based or procedure-based incoming port queue.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `check` ["(" (PortReceiveOp | PortGetCallOp | PortGetReplyOp | PortCatchOp) | ([`from` Address] ["->" [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]]) ")"].
requirements.original:
[ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." check
  [ "(" 
     ( PortReceiveOp | PortGetCallOp | PortGetReplyOp | PortCatchOp ) |
     ( [ from Address ] 
     [ "->" [ sender ValueRef] 
         [ @index value ValueRef] ] )
   ")" ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `check` operation IS an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original:
NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._ [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." check
  [ "(" 
     ( PortReceiveOp | PortGetCallOp | PortGetReplyOp | PortCatchOp ) |
     ( [ from Address ] 
     [ "->" [ sender ValueRef] 
         [ @index value ValueRef] ] )
   ")" ]

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation IS a generic operation that gives read access to the top element of a message-based or procedure-based incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The check operation is a generic operation that allows read access to the top element of message-based and procedure-based incoming port queues without removing the top element from the queue.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation SHALL NOT remove the top element from the incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The check operation is a generic operation that allows read access to the top element of message-based and procedure-based incoming port queues without removing the top element from the queue.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the port is message-based
requirements.canonical: At a message-based port, the `check` operation SHALL handle values of a certain type.
requirements.original: The check operation has to handle values of a certain type at message-based ports and to distinguish between calls to be accepted, exceptions to be caught and replies from previous calls at procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the port is procedure-based
requirements.canonical: At a procedure-based port, the `check` operation SHALL distinguish between calls to be accepted, exceptions to be caught and replies from previous calls.
requirements.original: The check operation has to handle values of a certain type at message-based ports and to distinguish between calls to be accepted, exceptions to be caught and replies from previous calls at procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation uses the receiving operations `receive`, `getcall`, `getreply` and `catch`, together with their matching and value, sender or parameter storing parts, to define the conditions to be checked and the information to be optionally extracted.
requirements.original: The receiving operations receive, getcall, getreply and catch together with their matching and value, sender or parameter storing parts, are used by the check operation to define the conditions that have to be checked and the information to be optionally extracted.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation SHALL check only the top element of an incoming port queue.
requirements.original: It is the top element of an incoming port queue that shall be checked (it is not possible to look into the queue).

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation CANNOT look into the incoming port queue beyond the top element.
requirements.original: It is the top element of an incoming port queue that shall be checked (it is not possible to look into the queue).

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the queue is empty
requirements.canonical: If the incoming port queue is empty, the `check` operation fails.
requirements.original: If the queue is empty the check operation fails.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the queue is not empty
requirements.canonical: If the incoming port queue is not empty, the `check` operation takes a copy of the top element and performs the specified receiving operation on the copy.
requirements.original: If the queue is not empty, a copy of the top element is taken and the receiving operation specified in the check operation is performed on the copy.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the receiving operation fails
requirements.canonical: If the receiving operation fails, i.e. the matching criteria are not fulfilled, the `check` operation fails.
requirements.original: The check operation fails if the receiving operation fails i.e. the matching criteria are not fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the check operation fails
requirements.canonical: If the `check` operation fails, the copy of the top element of the incoming port queue IS discarded.
requirements.original: In this case the copy of the top element of the queue is discarded and test execution continues in the normal manner, i.e. the statement or alternative next to the check operation is evaluated. The check operation fails if the receiving operation fails i.e. the matching criteria are not fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the check operation fails
requirements.canonical: If the `check` operation fails, test execution continues in the normal manner by evaluating the statement or alternative next to the `check` operation.
requirements.original: In this case the copy of the top element of the queue is discarded and test execution continues in the normal manner, i.e. the statement or alternative next to the check operation is evaluated. The check operation fails if the receiving operation fails i.e. the matching criteria are not fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the receiving operation is successful
requirements.canonical: If the receiving operation is successful, the `check` operation is successful.
requirements.original: The check operation is successful if the receiving operation is successful.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: the check operation is successful
requirements.canonical: If the `check` operation is successful, the value, sender or parameter storing parts of the receiving operation, if any, are executed, storing the message or a part of it, the sender's address or component reference, the parameters of the call or reply or the value of the exception in the associated variables.
requirements.original: In this case, the value, sender or parameter storing parts of the receiving operation, if any, are executed, i.e. the message and/or a part of it, the sender's address or component reference, the parameter(s) of the call or reply or the value of the exception are stored in the associated variables. The check operation is successful if the receiving operation is successful.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: check is used as a stand-alone statement
requirements.canonical: A stand-alone `check` statement IS a shorthand for an `alt` statement with the `check` operation as the only alternative.
requirements.original: If check is used as a stand-alone statement, it is considered to be a shorthand for an alt statement with the check operation as the only alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: one-to-many connections
requirements.canonical: In the case of one-to-many connections, the `check` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: In the case of one-to-many connections the check operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner. **Check from a specific sender**

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: A restriction of the `check` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted by the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: A one-to-one connection IS a simple case of a one-to-many connection, so the `from` clause MAY also be used with a `check` operation on a one-to-one connection.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:check-any-operation
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation with no argument list checks whether anything waits for processing in an incoming port queue.
requirements.original: A check operation with no argument list allows checking whether something waits for processing in an incoming port queue. **Check any operation**

requirements.subject: ent:check-any-operation
requirements.canonical: The check any operation MAY use a `from` clause to distinguish between different senders in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.original: The check any operation allows to distinguish between different senders (in case of one-to-many connections) by using a from clause and to retrieve the sender by using a shorthand assignment part with a sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:check-any-operation
requirements.canonical: The check any operation MAY retrieve the sender by a shorthand assignment part with a `sender` clause.
requirements.original: The check any operation allows to distinguish between different senders (in case of one-to-many connections) by using a from clause and to retrieve the sender by using a shorthand assignment part with a sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation on any port IS denoted by the `any port` keywords.
requirements.original: To check on any port, use the any port keywords. **Check on any port**

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation on any port of a specific port array IS denoted by the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.
requirements.original: To check on any port from a specific port array, indices use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier. **Check on any port from a port array**

ambiguity.issue: The phrase 'from a specific port array, indices use' is garbled; the word 'indices' appears to be an editorial leftover.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` PortArrayRef construct of a `check` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To check on any port from a specific port array, indices use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation on a single-dimensional port array MAY store the index of the port at which the operation was successful in a variable of type `integer`.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation on a multi-dimensional port array MAY store the index of the successful port in an integer array or `record of integer` variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: When a `check` operation checks a port array for a matching message, call, reply or exception, the `check` operation iterates the port indices from lowest to highest.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for a matching message, call, reply or exception, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.condition: the port array is multi-dimensional
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the `check` operation iterates over the ports from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Using the `check` operation in a wrong manner, e.g. checking for an exception at a message-based port, SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: a) Using the check operation in a wrong manner, e.g. check for an exception at a message-based port shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The clear port operation IS the port operation that empties incoming port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.condition: an ObjectReference is specified

requirements.original: The clear operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port or of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.condition: `all port` is used
requirements.canonical: When used with `all port`, the `clear` operation removes the contents of the incoming queues of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.
requirements.original: The clear operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port or of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port queue is already empty
requirements.canonical: If a port queue is already empty, the `clear` operation SHALL have no action on that port.
requirements.original: If a port queue is already empty then this operation shall have no action on that port.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `start` port operation enables sending and receiving operations on the port or ports it is applied to.
requirements.original: The start operation enables sending and receiving operations on the port(s).

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The start port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." start.
requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." start

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `start` operation clears the incoming queue of the named port.
requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive, getcall, etc. the start operation clears the incoming queue of the named port and starts listening for traffic over the port.

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `start` operation starts listening for traffic over the port.
requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive, getcall, etc. the start operation clears the incoming queue of the named port and starts listening for traffic over the port.

requirements.subject: ent:sending-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined to allow sending operations and has been started
requirements.canonical: If a port allows sending operations, after the `start` operation sending operations such as `send`, `call` and `raise` MAY be performed at that port.
requirements.original: If the port is defined to allow sending operations then the operations such as send, call, raise, etc. are also allowed to be performed at that port.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.condition: by default
requirements.canonical: All ports of a test component SHALL be started implicitly when the component is created.
requirements.original: By default, all ports of a component shall be started implicitly when a component is created.

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port is not stopped
requirements.canonical: A `start` operation applied to an unstopped port restarts the port by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
requirements.original: The start port operation will cause unstopped ports to be restarted by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.

readings: A `start` operation applied to an already started port restarts it by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
A `start` operation applied to a port that is not in the stopped state (started or halted) clears its incoming queue.
ambiguity.issue: 'unstopped ports' is not a defined port state; chose the reading that covers every non-stopped port (started or halted), consistent with NOTE 3 of 22.5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `start` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `stop` port operation disables sending operations at the port or ports it is applied to.
requirements.original: The stop operation disables sending and disallow receiving operations to match at the port(s).

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `stop` port operation disallows receiving operations to match at the port or ports it is applied to.
requirements.original: The stop operation disables sending and disallow receiving operations to match at the port(s).

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The stop port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." stop.
requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." stop

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `stop` operation causes listening at the named port to cease.
requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive and getcall, the stop operation causes listening at the named port to cease.

requirements.subject: ent:sending-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined to allow sending operations and has been stopped
requirements.canonical: If a port allows sending operations, sending operations such as `send`, `call` and `raise` SHALL NOT be performed at that port after a `stop` operation.
requirements.original: If the port is defined to allow sending operations then stop port disallows the operations such as send, call, raise, etc. to be performed.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: When a port is stopped, all receiving operations at that port performed before the `stop` operation SHALL be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.
requirements.original: To cease listening at the port means that all receiving operations defined before the stop operation shall be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.

readings: Receiving operations already executed (successfully matched) before the `stop` operation are completed, i.e. their effects (e.g. value redirections) take place.
Receiving operations that appear textually before the `stop` operation in the behaviour are performed completely before the port is suspended.
ambiguity.issue: 'defined before the stop operation' is unclear: executed before in time or written before in the code; chose the temporal execution reading.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `stop` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:halt-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `halt` port operation, unlike the `stop` port operation, allows entries already in the port queue to be processed with receiving operations.
requirements.original: The halt operation is comparable to the stop operation, but allows entries being already in the queue to be processed with receiving operations.

requirements.subject: ent:halt-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The halt port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." halt.
requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." halt

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.condition: the port allows receiving operations and has been halted
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, a receiving operation SHALL NOT succeed for messages and procedure call elements that enter the port queue after the `halt` operation was performed at that port.
requirements.original: If a port allows receiving operations such as receive, trigger and getcall, the halt operation disallows receiving operations to succeed for messages and procedure call elements that enter the port queue after performing the halt operation at that port.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: A receiving operation CAN process messages and procedure call elements that were already in the port queue before the `halt` operation.
requirements.original: Messages and procedure call elements that were already in the queue before the halt operation can still be processed with receiving operations.

requirements.subject: ent:sending-operation
requirements.condition: the port allows sending operations and has been halted
requirements.canonical: If a port allows sending operations, sending operations such as `send`, `call` and `raise` SHALL NOT be performed at that port immediately after the `halt` operation.
requirements.original: If the port allows sending operations then halt port immediately disallows sending operations such as send, call, raise, etc. to be performed.

requirements.subject: ent:halt-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port has already been halted
requirements.canonical: A `halt` operation on an already halted port has no effect on the state of the port or its queue.
requirements.original: Subsequent halt operations have no effect on the state of the port or its queue.

requirements.subject: ent:halt-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `halt` port operation virtually puts a marker after the last entry in the port queue received when the operation is performed.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The port halt operation virtually puts a marker after the last entry in the queue received when the operation is performed.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: Port queue entries ahead of the halt marker CAN be processed normally.
requirements.original: Entries ahead of the marker can be processed normally.

requirements.subject: ent:port-state
requirements.condition: all entries ahead of the marker have been processed
requirements.canonical: After all port queue entries ahead of the halt marker have been processed, the state of a halted port IS equivalent to the stopped state.
requirements.original: After all entries in the queue ahead of the marker have been processed, the state of the port is equivalent to the stopped state.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.condition: a stop operation is performed on a halted port with unprocessed entries ahead of the marker

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation

requirements.original: NOTE 3: A port start operation on a halted port clears all entries in the queue irrespectively if they arrived before or after performing the port halt operation.

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.canonical: A `start` operation on a halted port removes the halt marker.
requirements.original: It also removes the marker.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation

requirements.original: NOTE 4: A port clear operation on a halted port clears all entries in the queue irrespectively if they arrived before or after performing the port halt operation.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.canonical: A `clear` operation on a halted port virtually puts the halt marker at the top of the port queue.
requirements.original: It also virtually puts the marker at the top of the queue.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation

requirements.original: The checkstate port operation allows to check the state of a port.

requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) | ( any port )) "." checkstate "(" SingleExpression ")"

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation

requirements.original: If a port is in the state specified by the parameter, the checkstate operation returns the Boolean value true.

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation
requirements.condition: the port is not in the specified state
requirements.canonical: If a port is not in the state specified by the parameter, the `checkstate` operation returns the boolean value `false`.
requirements.original: If the port is not in the specified state, the checkstate operation returns the Boolean value false.

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation

requirements.original: Calling the checkstate operation with an invalid argument leads to an error.

requirements.original: It allows to check if a port is Started, Halted or Stopped, but also if a port is Connected, Mapped or Linked (i.e. Connected or Mapped).

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation

requirements.original: 4) "Connected"

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation

requirements.original: 5) "Mapped"

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation MAY have the value "Linked".
requirements.original: 6) "Linked"

requirements.canonical: Clause E.2.2.4 defines the type `objState` and the constants STARTED, HALTED, STOPPED, CONNECTED, MAPPED and LINKED for use with the `checkstate` operation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Clause E.2.2.4 includes the type definition objState and the constant definitions STARTED, HALTED,STOPPED, CONNECTED, MAPPED, and LINKED.

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `checkstate` operation SHOULD be used in combination with the `objState` type and its constants defined in clause E.2.2.4.

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation
requirements.condition: the parameter value is not in the allowed list
requirements.canonical: Calling the `checkstate` operation with a `charstring` parameter value other than "Started", "Halted", "Stopped", "Connected", "Mapped" or "Linked" SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: b) Calling the checkstate operation with a charstring parameter not listed in a) shall lead to an error.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `checkstate` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: c) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:any-keyword
requirements.canonical: The keywords `any` and `all` MAY be used with port configuration and communication operations only as indicated in table 26.
requirements.original: The keywords any and all may be used with configuration and communication operations as indicated in table 26.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: Ports are owned by test components and instantiated when the owning test component is created.
requirements.original: NOTE: Ports are owned by test components and instantiated when a component is created.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: `any port` and `all port` address all ports owned by a test component, not only the ports known in the scope of the function or altstep executed on the component.
requirements.original: The keywords any port and all port address all ports owned by a test component and not only the ports known in the scope of the function or altstep that is executed on the component.
